questions.question: What is the second truth called?
questions.answer: It is called absolute dominicality.

questions.question: Where does this truth show up?
questions.answer: It shows up all through the universe, especially in living things.

questions.question: What kind of care is seen in living things?
questions.answer: They are raised and cared for with wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: What does the passage say this caring power proves?
questions.answer: It proves a complete and real lordship from Allah.

questions.question: Is this care easy to see in just one place, or in many places?
questions.answer: It is seen in many places.

questions.question: Are the ways things are cared for always expected by people?
questions.answer: No. They often happen in surprising ways.

questions.question: Why can this complete lordship not have a partner?
questions.answer: Because having a partner would ruin its goals.

questions.question: What are some of those goals?
questions.answer: Showing beauty, showing perfection, showing fine works, and showing hidden skills.

questions.question: In what kinds of things are those goals gathered closely?
questions.answer: In small details and in living things.

questions.question: What could happen if even a tiny thing were linked to a partner with Allah?
questions.answer: Those goals would be blocked and damaged.

questions.question: What bad change would happen in people’s hearts if they turned to causes instead of Allah?
questions.answer: They would turn away from Allah and from His wise purposes.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an help people understand Allah’s oneness here?
questions.answer: It keeps pointing people to Allah’s purity and oneness in a guiding way.

questions.question: What main idea is taught in this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s lordship over everything is complete and has no partner.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give of Allah’s work in the universe?
questions.answer: A hidden, caring, and wise power is working everywhere.

questions.question: Which part of creation is named in a special way?
questions.answer: Living things are named in a special way.

questions.question: What happens to living things in this passage?
questions.answer: They are fed, grown, and looked after.

questions.question: What two qualities describe this care?
questions.answer: It is wise and compassionate.

questions.question: If the same kind of care is seen everywhere, what can we understand?
questions.answer: One Lord is caring for all of it.

questions.question: Why would sharing this lordship with another be wrong?
questions.answer: Because true lordship does not allow sharing.

questions.question: What beautiful things does this lordship want to show?
questions.answer: Beauty, perfection, fine art, and hidden wonders.

questions.question: Where can these beautiful things be seen clearly?
questions.answer: In small things and in living creatures.

questions.question: If people thought causes did everything, what would they forget?
questions.answer: They would forget Allah and His purposes.

questions.question: Would that agree with true lordship or go against it?
questions.answer: It would go against it.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an’s words and even its letters?
questions.answer: They guide people again and again to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What truth is being explained in this part?
questions.answer: The truth of absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What does dominicality mean here in a simple way?
questions.answer: It means Allah takes care of and rules His creation.

questions.question: How wide is Allah’s caring rule in this passage?
questions.answer: It reaches everywhere in the universe.

questions.question: What shows this rule most clearly?
questions.answer: The care and growth of living things.

questions.question: How are these works done?
questions.answer: They are done with wisdom, mercy, and in wonderful ways.

questions.question: What does the passage say about a partner in this rule?
questions.answer: A partner cannot be accepted.

questions.question: Why would even a small partnership be harmful?
questions.answer: Because it would spoil great goals seen in even tiny living things.

questions.question: Name one goal of this rule.
questions.answer: One goal is to show beauty.

questions.question: Name another goal of this rule.
questions.answer: Another goal is to show perfection.

questions.question: What else does this rule show besides beauty and perfection?
questions.answer: It shows precious works and hidden abilities.

questions.question: What happens if people look only at causes?
questions.answer: Their attention turns away from Allah.

questions.question: According to the passage, what keeps guiding people to tawhid, the oneness of Allah?
questions.answer: The Qur’an keeps guiding people to it.

questions.question: What title does the passage give to the second truth?
questions.answer: Absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What kind of hand is described in the passage?
questions.answer: A hidden hand that is wise and caring.

questions.question: What is this hand doing in the universe?
questions.answer: It is working everywhere.

questions.question: What does it do for living things?
questions.answer: It helps them grow and gives them care.

questions.question: Is this work random or full of meaning?
questions.answer: It is full of meaning.

questions.question: What does such meaningful care prove about Allah?
questions.answer: It proves His real and complete lordship.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention tiny details and living beings?
questions.answer: Because the signs of Allah’s care and art are gathered there.

questions.question: If someone says a cause or partner did these things, what would that hurt?
questions.answer: It would hurt the purposes of Allah’s lordship.

questions.question: What are people not supposed to turn toward instead of Allah?
questions.answer: They are not supposed to turn toward causes as if causes are the real doers.

questions.question: Why is that turning away a serious mistake?
questions.answer: Because it fights against the meaning of Allah’s lordship.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Qur’an often declares?
questions.answer: It often declares Allah’s holiness and greatness above partners.

questions.question: What do those Qur’anic teachings act like for people?
questions.answer: They act like guides to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What is one big sign of Allah’s lordship in this passage?
questions.answer: The care, growth, and training of living things.

questions.question: How often is this sign seen?
questions.answer: It is seen all across the universe.

questions.question: What feeling do the words wise and compassionate give about this care?
questions.answer: They show that the care is thoughtful and kind.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way this care appears?
questions.answer: It appears in similar ways everywhere, yet it is still surprising.

questions.question: What truth does this surprising care point to?
questions.answer: It points to Allah’s absolute lordship.

questions.question: Can absolute lordship be shared?
questions.answer: No. It cannot be shared at all.

questions.question: What are some special things this lordship wants to make known?
questions.answer: Beauty, perfection, art, and hidden wonders.

questions.question: In what places are these shown in a focused way?
questions.answer: In particular things and in living beings.

questions.question: If a partner were imagined, what would happen to those special purposes?
questions.answer: They would be broken and lost.

questions.question: What wrong direction might conscious beings take then?
questions.answer: They might look to causes instead of Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe that wrong direction?
questions.answer: It says it goes against the very nature of true lordship.

questions.question: What part of the Qur’an is said to guide people to Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: Its verses, words, letters, and even the shapes of the letters.

questions.question: What is the name of the truth in this passage?
questions.answer: The truth of absolute dominicality.

questions.question: What does the passage ask us to notice in the world?
questions.answer: The caring work spread throughout the whole universe.

questions.question: Which creatures are given special attention in this caring work?
questions.answer: Living creatures are given special attention.

questions.question: What two beautiful qualities are joined with this caring work?
questions.answer: Wisdom and mercy.

questions.question: What can we learn from seeing this kind of care everywhere?
questions.answer: We can learn that Allah alone is the Lord over all.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s lordship called absolute in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it is complete and reaches all things.

questions.question: What important aims belong to this lordship?
questions.answer: Showing beauty, perfection, fine works, and hidden skills.

questions.question: Why are even small living things important in the passage?
questions.answer: Because those aims are shown in them too.

questions.question: What would happen if even the smallest thing were said to belong to a partner with Allah?
questions.answer: It would ruin the meaning and goals of Allah’s lordship.

questions.question: What is wrong with turning hearts toward causes?
questions.answer: It pulls hearts away from Allah, who planned those purposes.

questions.question: Does the passage present this as friendly to true lordship or against it?
questions.answer: It presents it as against true lordship.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an serve people in this part of the text?
questions.answer: It serves as a steady guide to Allah’s oneness.
